Malicious Supply-Chain Indicators

No confirmed malicious supply-chain indicators.

Automatic Execution Paths

  • pyproject.toml uses the standard setuptools.build_meta backend and setuptools.dynamic.version = { attr = "pyoaev.__version__" }. In the provided code, there is no evidence of malicious install-time command execution, .pth, sitecustomize.py, usercustomize.py, or malicious PEP 517 build hooks.
  • scripts/release.py contains top-level argparse.parse_args(), os.system(...), and GitHub API calls, but it appears to be a release automation script. There is no evidence that it is wired to run during installation, interpreter startup, or package import.
  • pyoaev/__init__.py imports several modules, but within the provided material there is no evidence of malicious import-time behavior.

Theft / Exfiltration / Persistence / Lateral Movement / Obfuscation

  • Credential harvesting: no evidence of broad discovery of environment variables, .env files, SSH keys, cloud/CI tokens, wallet files, or similar secrets.
  • Exfiltration: aside from normal API-client behavior and GitHub API use in the release script, there is no evidence of harvested-data upload, webhooks, raw IP endpoints, or paste/drop services.
  • Staging: no evidence of archiving, encoding, or temporary staging of stolen files.
  • Persistence: no cron, systemd, launch agents, shell profile modification, or self-reinstall loop evidence.
  • Lateral movement: no evidence involving Kubernetes service-account tokens, Docker socket access, cloud metadata, or CI workflow injection.
  • Obfuscation/loader behavior: base64.b64decode in helpers.py appears to decode signature values and is not tied to eval/exec/compile, a dynamic loader, or execution of an obfuscated payload.

Distribution Integrity Anomalies

  • Based on SOURCES.txt, the package contents appear to be a Python API client with documentation, tests, and a release script. No hidden payload, unexplained native binary, .pth file, or similar anomaly was confirmed.
  • The dependency list does not show clear typosquatting, suspicious newly inserted dependencies, or install/post-install execution behavior.
  • Wheel/sdist mismatch cannot be assessed because only the sdist content was provided.
